relates to Prometheus in physical terms); Ione is more timid, shy and inexperienced (she looks to
Panthea for explanation of events and characters), and also more sensitive and alert, embodying
innocent and purer forms of human love, such as altruism. The sisters appear to begin to merge
into each other, and then into Asia, from Act II. The names Panthea and Ione have no obvious
significance: S. consistently gives to characters who embody a distinctive departure from the
source myth names which cannot be pinned down within any received framework of meaning.
